title: spec review: S1b cache_telemetry: per-invocation prompt-cache economics (hit ratio, effective cost, prefix identity) from existing run rows and packet metadata (P6)
spec:
Create orchestrator/cache_telemetry.py. normalize(provider, usage) -> dict(input_uncached, cache_read, cache_write, output, hit_ratio) where hit_ratio = cache_read / (input_uncached + cache_read + cache_write) or 0.0; Claude usage keys input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, output_tokens; Codex keys input_tokens (includes cached), cached_input_tokens, output_tokens (see bus.py usage normalization around line 224 and executor.py around line 113; reuse, do not duplicate the semantics). effective_cost(norm, cfg) = input_uncached + cache_read*read_ratio + cache_write*write_ratio + output*output_ratio in token-equivalents, with per-provider ratios from pool.toml [cache] (new section: claude_read_ratio default 0.1, claude_write_ratio 1.25, codex_read_ratio 0.25, codex_write_ratio 1.0, output_ratio 5.0; add the section with dated comments).
Prefix identity: in orchestrator/spawn.py packet_meta (and the meta remembered by _remember_packet_meta) add prefix_sha (sha256 first 12 hex of the rendered role template text up to and including the first packet section that is task-specific, i.e. everything before the objective section), prefix_chars, suffix_chars and dynamic_sections (names of sections after the prefix). Do not reorder or change any section content in this task (stage 2 does). Also make bus.log_run rows (already written by spawn/executor with usage) carry cache fields: input_uncached_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, hit_ratio, effective_tokens, prefix_sha when available, via a single helper cache_telemetry.annotate(row) called from bus.log_run (guard: never raise from log_run).
report(root, days=7) -> per role and per provider: runs, input_uncached, cache_read, cache_write, hit_ratio, effective_tokens, distinct prefix_sha count and the share of runs whose prefix_sha was seen before within the window (reuse_rate); plus per goal totals. CLI: `orchestrator scorecard --cache [--days n] [--json]` (extend the existing scorecard subcommand in cli.py). The report must run on this repository's real .orchestrator/runs/*.jsonl rows (they exist for 2026-09-17..23; rows before this task lack prefix_sha and count as unknown prefix). Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/02-cache-telemetry.md with the definitions and the numbers measured on the real rows.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. Read docs/context-economy/00-overview.md only if you need the evidence/decision_log conventions.
acceptance: tests/test_cache_telemetry.py::test_effective_cost_uses_pool_ratios (ratios from a temp pool.toml; defaults when the section is absent)
tests/test_cache_telemetry.py::test_report_groups_by_role_provider_and_prefix_reuse (synthetic rows with repeated prefix_sha give reuse_rate)
tests/test_spawn.py::test_packet_meta_carries_prefix_identity (prefix_sha stable when only task-specific sections change)
tests/test_bus.py::test_log_run_annotates_cache_fields (row gets cache fields; annotate failure never raises)

risks.issue: Prefix definition self-contradicts: 'up to and including the first task-specific section' vs 'everything before the objective section' pick opposite boundaries. objective (spawn.py:589-593) is the first task-specific section, so including it makes prefix_sha vary per task, breaking the 'stable when only task-specific sections change' acceptance test.

Spec assumes .orchestrator/runs/*.jsonl for 2026-09-17..23 exists 'on this repository', but that data only exists in the main checkout, not in task worktrees (git worktree add only checks out committed files; runs/*.jsonl is uncommitted generated state). The executor's actual working directory has no runs data to measure.

Even granting access to the real rows, none of them have prefix_sha (all predate this task), so reuse_rate over the stated window is vacuous (100% unknown-prefix), not a meaningful baseline as the spec implies.

bus.log_run:353 already writes input_uncached_tokens/cache_read_tokens/cache_write_tokens/output_tokens via normalize_usage. cache_telemetry.normalize() is specified with differently-named keys (no _tokens suffix). Spec doesn't say whether annotate(row) reuses the already-computed row fields or recomputes independently, risking duplicate/divergent key sets on the same row.
Existing scorecard mode mutual-exclusivity check (line 216-217) isn't mentioned; --cache's interaction with it (included or deliberately exempt) is undefined.

suggested_spec_changes: Define the prefix boundary as exactly one of: 'everything before (not including) the first task-specific/objective section' — drop the contradictory 'up to and including' phrasing.

State explicitly that the cache-telemetry doc's numbers may show mostly/entirely unknown-prefix for the initial real-row window, since prefix_sha is new, and clarify whether the report should read runs data from the main repo checkout or is expected to be near-empty in a worktree.

Specify whether cache_telemetry.annotate(row) should reuse bus.py's already-normalized *_tokens fields or independently recompute from raw usage, and reconcile the two key-naming conventions (normalize()'s input_uncached/cache_read/cache_write/output vs bus's *_tokens suffixed keys).
Say whether --cache should be added to cli.py's existing scorecard mode mutual-exclusivity tuple (line 216).
